findings.F1: Inside the trend regime (forecast > 0), a down day bigger than half the coin's 20-day daily standard deviation was followed by a next-day mean return of +0.61%. This is averaged across coins per day, then tested over 516 independent days: t = 2.95. That is about twice the next-day return after an ordinary active day (+0.30%, t = 2.11, 1052 days) or an up day (+0.28%, t = 1.80, 808 days).
findings.F2: The bounce after a down day shows up in all 6 coins and in 7 of 8 years. In every coin, the next-day mean after a down day (+0.27% to +0.83%) is above the mean after other days (−0.14% to +0.10%). The only year where it is not higher is 2024 (+0.08% vs +0.30%). Outside the trend regime the bounce is weaker: +0.32%, t = 1.98, over 1000 days.
findings.F3: Measured per bar rather than per day, the same reversal holds. Moves between −1.5 and −0.5 standard deviations were followed by +0.47% the next day (t = 5.05, 2977 coin-days, not independent across coins). Moves between +0.5 and +2.5 standard deviations were followed by −0.04% and +0.18%, neither different from 0.
findings.F4: The 20-day trend edge itself is weak, which agrees with the verdict. Active 20-bar blocks earned an excess of +2.1% (t = 0.93, 262 blocks). Blocks where both the 60-day and 20-day returns were positive earned +3.3% (t = 1.50, 141 blocks).
findings.F5: The book's profit comes from the few trades that last. The 1019 trades held 3 days or less (40% of all trades) lost about −3.6% each. The 787 trades held more than 10 days averaged +10.5% (10–30 days) and +87.8% (over 30 days). The median trade is negative in every coin.
findings.F6: The next-day return following a weekday-4 bar was +0.37% when averaged across coins per day (t = 2.31, 345 days). Weekday-3 and weekday-4 bars together beat the other weekdays in 5 of 6 coins and 6 of 8 years. This is the strongest of 7 weekdays tested, so it is weaker evidence than F1.

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 20-day and 60-day returns are both positive, a daily close that falls by more than half its recent daily standard deviation is followed by an above-average return over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trend follower should add to, or enter, its long on a down day inside an uptrend rather than on an up day.
ideas.name: buy dips inside uptrends

ideas.idea: In any regime, a coin's large down day is followed by a next-day return above the coin's average, while a large up day is not.
ideas.consequence: A trader should avoid selling, or opening shorts, right after a sharp down day, since the next day tends to bounce.
ideas.name: one-day rebound after drops

ideas.idea: A coin's return over the day after a weekday-4 bar is higher than its return after the other weekdays' bars.
ideas.consequence: A long holder should prefer to be in the market over that day and to delay exits until after it.
ideas.name: late-week daily drift
